Congratulations to the Laredo Barracuda Swim Team!

On Sunday, Kassandra Herrera from my office attended the Laredo Parks and Leisure Fall Invitational USA Swim Meet and presented Congressional Recognitions to 98 Barracuda swimmers.

Thank you to Coach Kane and the swim team https://t.co/UGjeOE8mel

Meet Jake, one of our Fall 2026 interns in my Washington, D.C. Office! 

Jake is recent graduate of Xavier University, he majored in the Philosophy, Politics, and the Public Honors Program. Following his graduation, Jake moved to Washington D.C. to learn about representing rural https://t.co/1z3C4fpAk2

Last week, my Outreach Coordinator, Frida Figueroa, attended San Isidro Elementary’s Lone Star Ribbon School Ceremony. 

It was a wonderful opportunity to connect with Principal Adamina Meza, Superintendent Dr. Gerardo Cruz, and UISD Board of Trustees, Leticia Juarez, Victor https://t.co/KjmQA0qiCm

Recently, my Outreach Coordinator, Frida Figueroa, attended the grand opening of Laredo’s newest Goodwill location, marking the company’s third location in the city.

It was a pleasure to celebrate this milestone alongside President and CEO Carlos Contreras and the Goodwill team. We appreciate their warm welcome and continued commitment to serving the Laredo community.

Congratulations to the entire Goodwill team on this exciting addition to our community and thank you for investing in our community and helping create new opportunities for Laredo.

Good to join my colleagues in the Texas Democratic Congressional Delegation, Senator-elect James Talarico, and my daughter Christina as we prepare for the next session of Congress.

As the incoming dean of the Texas Democratic delegation, I look forward to working with both new and returning members to address the issues facing Texans across our state.

We have important work ahead of us, and I will continue making sure South Texas has a strong voice in Washington.

Good to see former Texas Congressman Ted Poe, who stopped by my Washington office.

Ted and I came into Congress together, and it's always good to reconnect with former colleagues. https://t.co/3bzcEqzgHp

Reports of migrants traveling north through Mexico following last week's election have raised questions about U.S. border policy.

Let me be clear: The election results have not changed our immigration laws. The border is not open to illegal entry, and there is no open-border policy.

I support strong border security and enforcing our immigration laws, with a focus on criminals and individuals who pose a threat to public safety. At the same time, we must continue working toward practical, bipartisan immigration solutions that support our economy and communities across the nation.

https://t.co/FIbo8qtufV

The House passed the bipartisan Major Richard Star Act (H.R. 2102) yesterday morning, which I supported to end the “wounded veteran tax.”

Combat-injured veterans who were forced to medically retire should not have to choose between their military retirement pay and VA disability compensation. This bill would allow eligible veterans to receive both benefits in full.

Our veterans have earned these benefits through their service and sacrifice. I urge the Senate to pass this legislation so we can get it signed into law.

This week, I welcomed the South Texas Builders Association (STBA) to Washington, D.C., to discuss practical immigration solutions that strengthen border security, support our workforce, and grow our economy.

We joined lawmakers and business leaders for a press conference at the Capitol, and I brought STBA's priorities directly to House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries. We also met with Rep. Pete Aguilar alongside Valley Interfaith to discuss the challenges facing South Texas families and businesses.

I will continue working with my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to advance commonsense immigration solutions that support our economy while keeping our border secure.

Thank you to STBA and Valley Interfaith for coming to Washington and making sure South Texas voices are heard.

Following our immigration press conference at the U.S. Capitol, I brought leaders from the South Texas Builders Association (STBA) to meet with House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries.

We discussed the importance of addressing immigration and economic issues affecting South https://t.co/rPxQPA60Ns

I met with representatives from the Permit America to Build Coalition to discuss bipartisan efforts to improve the federal permitting process.

Delays in federal permitting can hold up important energy and infrastructure projects, increase costs, and make it harder for businesses https://t.co/D2JkFZVF0U

I joined @RubenGallego, fellow Texas lawmakers, and member elects as well as the South Texas Builders Association (STBA) at the U.S. Capitol to discuss the need for bipartisan immigration reform.

We need practical solutions that strengthen border security, support American https://t.co/pTLrmeXyQN

Today I met with Dr. Albert Reyes and his team from Buckner International to discuss affordable housing in the Rio Grande Valley. 

Working in Peñitas, Buckner International has built new homes for communities at need. 

I’m looking forward to following their work and https://t.co/5Tx484dRV0

Yesterday, I met with Goldy Hyder, CEO of the Business Council of Canada, to talk about the future of trade between Texas and Canada. 

Texas’s relationship with Canada is vital to South Texas businesses, especially to our motor parts industry. I’m looking forward to more talks https://t.co/m2Tbql4QJq

As we prepare for the next Congress, I am honored to become the incoming dean of the Texas Democratic delegation.

I want to thank Congressman Lloyd Doggett for his years of service and leadership in this role.

I also had the opportunity to welcome six incoming members of our https://t.co/X9FXXzzXGe

Happy Veterans Day to all the men and women who have served our country!

I especially want to recognize our veterans here in South Texas and thank them for their service and sacrifices.

We have a responsibility to make sure our veterans receive the VA benefits, health care, and https://t.co/RnahqLZpqe

I was glad to join my fellow Blue Dog Democrats today for our coalition photo ahead of the next Congress.

It was good to see familiar faces and welcome new members, especially those from South Texas.

I look forward to working with our 14 incoming members from across the country, from Arizona to New Jersey, and wish them the best as they prepare to take office.

I welcomed Mexican Senator Néstor Camarillo Medina to the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C.

Senator Camarillo chairs the Mexican Senate’s Commission on Circular Economy and Business Development. We discussed opportunities to support small businesses, strengthen economic development, and continue cooperation between the United States and Mexico.

As Co-Chair of the U.S.-Mexico Interparliamentary Group, I know how important our relationship with Mexico is, especially for trade and economic growth in South Texas.

I also had the opportunity to show Senator Camarillo the view from the Speaker’s Balcony at the U.S. Capitol.

Thank you, Senator Camarillo, for visiting and for the productive conversation!

Meet Ayaan, one of our Fall 2026 interns in my Washington, D.C. office!

Ayaan is a senior at the University of Texas Rio Grande Valley (UTRGV), where he is studying Political Science with a minor in Legal Studies.

This semester, Ayaan is participating in the University of Texas System’s Archer Fellowship Program, which gives students the opportunity to live, study, and gain professional experience in Washington, D.C.

I am glad to have Ayaan on our team this fall and look forward to seeing him put his knowledge and skills to work while gaining firsthand experience serving the people of Texas’ 28th Congressional District!

It was good to spend some time with members of the South Texas Builders Association (STBA) at the U.S. Capitol!

I had the opportunity to introduce them to several of my fellow Blue Dog Democrats and show them around the Capitol, including the Speaker's Balcony.

Tomorrow, we'll join fellow lawmakers for a press conference to discuss practical immigration solutions that support American businesses, address workforce needs, and maintain strong border security.

Thank you to STBA for making the trip to Washington, D.C.!

Happy 251st Birthday to the United States Marine Corps!

On November 10, 1775, the Second Continental Congress established the Continental Marines, beginning a proud legacy of honor, courage, and commitment.

Today, we honor all Marines, past and present, for their service and sacrifice in defense of our nation. Thank you to our Marine families for standing alongside them.

Semper Fidelis!

It was great to see Sister Norma Pimentel and leaders from Valley Interfaith at the U.S. Capitol!

I had the opportunity to show them around the Capitol during their visit to Washington, D.C.

Thank you to Sister Norma and Valley Interfaith for the work you do to support families and communities across the Rio Grande Valley. It is always good to see familiar faces from South Texas in Washington!

The bipartisan Veterans’ Compensation Cost-of-Living Adjustment Act of 2026, has passed the House.

This important legislation will provide an annual cost-of-living adjustment for veterans receiving disability compensation and surviving family members receiving benefits. https://t.co/72AW3uEpaB

I am disappointed by the Supreme Court's decision to allow border barrier construction to move forward in the Big Bend region, including Big Bend National Park.

Earlier this year, I introduced an amendment to prohibit federal funding for border wall construction in Big Bend National Park, Big Bend Ranch State Park, and several areas in South Texas.

I have always supported securing our southern border, but that does not mean building a wall everywhere. Big Bend is one of Texas' greatest natural treasures, and we need to protect it.

We can have strong border security without damaging our national parks, historic sites, and surrounding communities.

https://t.co/mg6moiMXY5

My Outreach Coordinator, Frida Figueroa, attended the 19th Annual World Pugilist Hall of Fame ceremony this morning to recognize six new inductees.

My office honored each inductee with a Congressional Certificate of Recognition for their accomplishments and contributions to the sport of boxing.

Congratulations to all six inductees on this well-deserved recognition!

Thank you to Paul Buitron and everyone involved in organizing this year's ceremony and celebrating the accomplishments of these individuals.

My Outreach Coordinator, Kassandra Herrera, recently attended the Trail of Hope Press Conference in the City Council Chambers.

The press conference highlighted an opportunity for our community to come together to honor our veterans and bring awareness to mental health and suicide prevention. It was a pleasure joining City Council member, Vanessa Perez, Mayor Dr. Trevino, Awareness Warriors Foundation founder, Randy Villanueva, and our veteran community.

Thank you to everyone involved for their continued dedication to honoring our veterans, promoting mental health awareness, and supporting suicide prevention efforts. Together, we can continue to make a difference and remind our veterans that they are never alone.

Happy Election Day! 🗳️

Voting is one of the most important ways we can make our voices heard and have a say in the decisions that affect our communities.

I encourage all eligible South Texans to exercise their right to vote and participate in our democracy.

Thank you to the poll workers and election officials across South Texas who help make our elections possible!

My Outreach Coordinator, Frida Figueroa, recently attended the Women’s City Club kickoff fundraiser event for Pennies for Tennies. During this event, Dr. Ronald B. Newton was also recognized for his retirement and 26 years of dedication and partnership in serving the children of Laredo.

It was a pleasure connecting with Women’s City Club leadership, Mayor Dr. Victor Treviño, Councilman Tyler King, Commissioner Wawi Tijerina, and Sandy Salinas with Communities In Schools.

Thank you to the Women’s City Club for the invitation and for your continued commitment to making a difference in the lives of local children. We are grateful for the opportunity to support organizations that invest in our community’s future and look forward to continuing these meaningful partnerships.

Meet Jaden, one of our Fall 2026 interns in my Washington, D.C. office!

Jaden is a senior at Texas Tech University, where she studies Natural Resource Management with a concentration in Conservation Science.

Through her studies, Jaden has gained an appreciation for the role of agriculture, environmental conservation, and public policy in our communities. She hopes to use her background in science to help address issues affecting our natural resources.

I am glad to have Jaden on our team this fall and look forward to seeing her put her knowledge and skills to work while gaining firsthand experience serving the people of Texas' 28th Congressional District.

Recently, my Outreach Coordinator, Kassandra Herrera, visited the Larga Vista Community Center during their weekly crafts session to share information about the services my office provides.

Kassandra spoke with residents about how my office can assist with federal agencies and helped connect constituents with our team for additional assistance.

Thank you to the staff at Larga Vista Community Center for welcoming us and to everyone who took the time to visit with Kassandra!

If you need assistance with a federal agency, my office is here to help.

Even Halloween candy is getting more expensive.

A new analysis found that prices for popular Halloween candies have increased 15.3% over the past year, more than four times the overall inflation rate.

South Texas families are already paying more for groceries, gas, and other https://t.co/KEbhes2TLs

Health insurance is becoming more expensive for American families, and another round of premium increases is coming in 2027.

According to new data from KFF, Affordable Care Act marketplace premiums for benchmark plans are set to increase by an average of 13% nationwide next year, following a 26% increase in 2026. The expiration of enhanced federal tax credits has also left many families paying more for coverage.

For South Texans who purchase their own health insurance, including small business owners, self-employed workers, and families without employer-sponsored coverage, these rising costs can put an even greater strain on household budgets.

Families are already paying more for groceries, housing, and utilities. They should not have to worry about whether they can afford to keep their health insurance, too.

Congress needs to address rising premiums and make health care more affordable. I will continue working to protect access to coverage and help South Texas families get the care they need.

https://t.co/CzqfzNqDtT

Earlier this month, my Coordinator, Brandon Rockers, attended the Toys for Tots kickoff hosted by Laredo ISD and the Marine Corps Reserve to start the season of giving.

During the event, Marine combat veteran Dr. Hignio Reyes presented the Honorary Marine Award to Councilman Gilbert Gonzalez and Jose Gonzalez, LPC. Congratulations to both on this recognition.

Thank you to Laredo ISD, the Marine Corps Reserve, and everyone who came out to support Toys for Tots and help bring gifts to children in our community this holiday season.

Young people in La Salle County deserve a safe, welcoming place to spend their time.

In the House-passed FY27 Agriculture Appropriations bill, I secured $938,000 in Community Project Funding for improvements to the La Salle County Youth Center in Cotulla. This funding would help the county upgrade the center so it can continue serving young people and families in the community.

I will continue working to support rural communities like Cotulla.

This morning, my Outreach Coordinator, Brandon Rockers, joined Lamar Middle School students and the Laredo Police Department for a GEAR UP event with the LPD Explorer Program.

Students took part in a mock police fitness test, which included a mile-and-a-half run, push-ups, sit-ups, and an obstacle course. Programs like GEAR UP help students start thinking early about college and their future careers.

Thank you to the Laredo Police Department Community Outreach Team and Lamar Middle School for giving these students a firsthand look at a career in law enforcement.

Today, we remember Sir Patrick Stewart, whose extraordinary talent brought generations together through stories of courage, compassion and hope. From Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek to Professor Charles Xavier in X-Men, his performances reminded us of the power of thoughtful leadership and seeing the best in others.

My condolences go out to his family, friends and fans around the world. His legacy on stage and screen will continue to inspire.

https://t.co/uvjHJVEg1q

I voted for the House-passed FY27 Military Construction and Veterans Affairs Appropriations bill, which includes report language supporting the Air https://t.co/Ai2CJki5hK

My Outreach Coordinator, Brandon Rockers, joined the Duval County community for the annual Halloween Block Party, where about 1,100 people came out to enjoy the evening.

Thank you to Duval County for hosting, and to Sheriff Romeo R. Ramirez, Mayor Sally Lichtenberger, Marty https://t.co/ykuItyYs4R

For many veterans in rural South Texas, home care makes it possible to receive the care they need while staying close to their families.

I voted for the House-passed FY27 Military Construction and Veterans Affairs Appropriations bill, which includes report language calling on the Department of Veterans Affairs to account for how changes to home care reimbursement affect veterans and providers in Texas and New Mexico.

Congress needs clear information on how these changes affect veterans' access to care and what can be done to prevent disruptions.

I will continue working to make sure South Texas veterans can keep receiving care at home.

Happy Birthday to Tojo Perez! 

Great to celebrate alongside Tony Salinas, Judge Meme Flores, and David Almarez. 

Wishing you a wonderful day surrounded by family and friends, and a year filled with good health, happiness, and blessings! https://t.co/nWISgP9bi2

In the FY27 appropriations package, I helped support $57.344 million for https://t.co/IzV23oAkhd

Today, I was proud to join the Jim Hogg County community in Hebbronville for the unveiling of the Vaquero Metal Art, a tribute honoring the past, present, and future vaqueros of Jim Hogg County.

A special thank you to Hebbronville Machine Shop for designing and donating this beautiful piece of artwork, and to everyone who helped bring this tribute to life.

I'm proud to celebrate the history, traditions, and hardworking men and women who have helped shape our South Texas communities!

Diabetes and kidney disease affect many families across South Texas, and medical research is key to finding better ways to prevent and treat them.

In the FY27 appropriations package, I helped support $2.3 billion for the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK), which funds research on diabetes, digestive diseases, kidney disease, and other chronic conditions.

This funding supports continued research on Type 1 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, Alpha-1 liver disease, and inflammatory bowel diseases such as Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis.

I will continue supporting medical research that leads to better treatment and care for South Texans living with chronic disease.

According to a new Pentagon estimate, the war in Iran has cost American taxpayers $47.1 billion, and that figure does not include damage to U.S. military bases in the Middle East.

I have been clear that I do not want to see an endless war. The administration needs to provide

I am saddened to hear of the passing of Dolores Huerta, a longtime labor leader and civil rights advocate.

As a co-founder of the United Farm Workers, she spent decades fighting for better wages, safer working conditions, and fair treatment for farmworkers and their families.

Her work made a difference for generations of working families, including many here in South Texas.

My thoughts and prayers are with her family, friends, and loved ones. May she rest in peace.

My Outreach Coordinator, Jesus Toro Martinez, recently joined the Seraphic Franciscan Sisters to celebrate their 50th anniversary of service to South Texas.

For five decades, the Sisters have dedicated themselves to helping those in need and supporting underserved communities across our region.

I was pleased to recognize their 50 years of service with a Congressional Certificate of Recognition.

Thank you to the Seraphic Franciscan Sisters for your continued dedication to the people of South Texas!

San Antonio is home to the 16th Air Force, which leads the Air Force's cyber and information warfare mission. The airmen and civilians who serve there work to defend our nation against cyber threats.

I voted for the House-passed FY27 Military Construction and Veterans Affairs https://t.co/NY0sn4Zehi

It was great to visit with constituents at Walmart this Sunday.

I also stopped to say hello to some of our local Cub Scouts and bought some popcorn to support their pack. Thank you to these young Scouts for working hard on their fundraiser! https://t.co/bJFRZrqUrI

Every season, South Texas farmers have to protect their crops from pests and plant disease while dealing with limited water.

In the House-passed FY27 Agriculture Appropriations bill, I helped secure a $500,000 increase for USDA research on aflatoxin, a toxin produced by mold https://t.co/FJAEadFtUJ

I am saddened to hear of the passing of former Texas State Representative Clint Hackney.

Clint and I served together in the Texas House of Representatives when I first took office in 1987. He dedicated many years of his life to public service, from serving our country in the

Today, I joined LLUSCBA for a conference highlighting the customs brokers and trade professionals who keep goods moving through our ports and support jobs on both sides of the border.

We discussed the importance of certainty under USMCA, modernizing our land ports, and https://t.co/0OdraP2uaa

Ranchers and landowners across South Texas rely on healthy livestock and wildlife. A disease outbreak or losses to predators can set an operation back for years.

In the House-passed FY27 Agriculture Appropriations bill, I helped secure $17.5 million to fight chronic wasting disease in deer, including $5 million for indemnity payments to remove infected and exposed animals.

The bill also provides $27.5 million for swine health, with a $500,000 increase for the Swine Health Improvement Program, and a $1 million increase for USDA Wildlife Services to improve predator management.

As a senior member of the House Appropriations Committee, I will continue working to protect South Texas livestock and the ranchers who raise them.

On Friday, I announced $6,381,000 in federal funding for Border Pacific Railroad Company to improve freight rail infrastructure between Rio Grande City and Mission.

Awarded through the Federal Railroad Administration’s Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) Program, this investment will help rehabilitate approximately six miles of track and 27 curves, improving safety, reliability and freight capacity. These upgrades will support local businesses and strengthen the movement of goods through Starr and Hidalgo counties.

Thank you to Sam Vale, Robert Vale and the Border Pacific Railroad team for their partnership and commitment to South Texas. I’ll continue working to bring federal resources home to improve our infrastructure and support our region’s economic growth!

For many South Texas students, especially those who are the first in their families to go to college, getting into college and paying for it can be difficult without the right support.

In the FY27 appropriations package, I supported $1.2 billion for Federal TRIO programs. TRIO helps students from low-income families, first-generation college students, and students with disabilities prepare for college and complete their education.

Here in South Texas, TRIO programs at Region One, UTSA, and UTRGV help students with coursework, college applications, and financial aid.

I will continue working to protect TRIO funding so more South Texas students can earn a college degree.

South Texas farmers and ranchers face challenges every day, from drought and crop pests to livestock diseases like New World screwworm. Agricultural research plays an important role in helping producers address these threats and protect their operations.

In the FY27 appropriations bill, I supported $1.795 billion for the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Agricultural Research Service to continue research that benefits farmers and ranchers across the country.

This funding would support efforts to improve crop yields, control agricultural pests, combat livestock diseases, and develop new ways to address the challenges facing our producers.

Agriculture is an important part of the South Texas economy, and our farmers and ranchers depend on reliable research to protect their crops, livestock, and livelihoods. I will continue working to support agricultural research and make sure our producers can benefit from these federal investments.

Happy birthday to my wonderful wife, Imelda! 

Thank you for always being by my side and for everything you do for our family. I am grateful for the life we've built together and all the wonderful memories we've made along the way.

Catherine, Christina, and I want to wish you a very happy birthday! Thank you for all the love and support you give our family.

Alzheimer's disease affects thousands of Texas families, including those caring for loved ones who need daily assistance. Finding reliable care and support can be difficult, especially for families in rural communities.

As part of the FY27 appropriations process, I supported $31.5 million for programs that help states improve Alzheimer's care and coordinate services for patients and their families.

This funding would help strengthen partnerships between health care providers, state agencies, and community organizations to make it easier for families to access services and get the assistance they need.

I will continue working to improve access to care and support South Texans living with Alzheimer's, along with the family members and caregivers who care for them every day.

Yesterday, I joined community members in Atascosa County for the Shine a Light Together Vigil, hosted by Safer Path Family Violence Shelter, to honor lives lost to domestic violence and stand with survivors.

The evening brought together advocates, law enforcement and local leaders in a shared commitment to prevention, survivor safety and accountability. Thank you to Andrea Rathmell, the Safer Path team and the survivors who courageously shared their stories.

Everyone deserves to feel safe in their home. Together, we can support those affected by domestic violence and work toward a safer future for our families.

In the FY27 appropriations bill, I supported $1.795 billion for the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Agricultural Research Service to continue research that benefits farmers and ranchers across the country.

This funding would support efforts to improve crop yields, control agricultural pests, combat livestock diseases, and develop new ways to address the challenges facing our producers.

Agriculture is an important part of the South Texas economy, and our farmers and ranchers depend on reliable research to protect their crops, livestock, and livelihoods. I will continue working to support agricultural research and make sure our producers can benefit from these federal investments.

Laredo is the nation's busiest port of entry, and South Texas needs a transportation system that can keep up with the movement of people and goods across our border.

In the BUILD America 250 Act, I secured language directing the U.S. Department of Transportation to consider a passenger rail route connecting Austin, San Antonio, and Laredo, with a possible extension to Monterrey, Mexico. This is an important step toward exploring new passenger rail service that could improve travel between these cities and strengthen our connections with Mexico.

The bill would also establish a freight data-sharing program to help ports, railroads, trucking companies, and shippers identify delays and improve the movement of goods. It also calls for a study of cybersecurity risks affecting the technology used to manage our transportation systems.

With so much trade moving through Laredo, we need to make sure our transportation infrastructure can handle growing demand. I will continue working to advance these provisions, improve transportation connections, and support the businesses and workers who depend on reliable transportation across South Texas.

Today, I was pleased to announce $5,725,000 in federal funding over five years for Serving Children and Adults in Need (SCAN) to expand mental health and substance use treatment services in South Texas.

Through the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, $3 million will support SCAN’s Children’s Hope and Healing Center in Laredo, providing trauma screenings, counseling and care for approximately 1,000 children and adolescents ages 2 to 17.

An additional $2.725 million will fund the Families United Project, helping adolescents and young adults overcome substance use disorders and co-occurring mental health conditions while involving their families in the recovery process.

Thank you to SCAN’s leadership, staff and community partners for more than 40 years of service to our region! I’ll continue working to bring federal resources home and improve access to care for South Texas families.

Families across South Texas are paying more for everyday necessities, and those additional costs are taking a toll on household budgets.

According to an analysis from the Joint Economic Committee Democrats, families in Texas's 28th Congressional District have faced thousands of dollars in higher costs for housing, groceries, energy, and health care.

The war in Iran has added to these financial pressures by driving up fuel prices. When gasoline and diesel cost more, families pay more at the pump, while truck drivers, farmers, ranchers, and small businesses face higher operating expenses. Those costs can also lead to higher prices for the goods and services families rely on.

For families, these increases mean less money left over after paying the bills. Congress needs to focus on lowering energy costs, addressing rising household expenses, and providing relief to the families and businesses struggling with higher prices.

I will continue working across the aisle to address these costs and protect the financial well-being of South Texas families.

With more than 150 exhibitors, the expo brings together businesses, families, and community members to showcase products, services, and the creativity that makes Laredo special.

Thank you to the organizers and participating businesses for bringing our community together. I remain committed to supporting small businesses and expanding opportunities for South Texas families!

I was pleased to join Azteca neighborhood residents, the Rio Grande International Study Center, and community volunteers at Las Palmas for the 32nd Día del Río.

During the event, I received a petition signed by hundreds of community members raising concerns about proposed border wall construction and its potential impact on their homes, flood risk, river access, and the future of Las Palmas. Their voices deserve to be heard in Washington as we work to secure our border while protecting our neighborhoods and natural resources.

Thank you to the residents, volunteers, and community partners working to restore this treasured greenspace and protect the Rio Grande. I will continue fighting for transparency, public safety, and the preservation of South Texas for future generations!

The Rio Grande is one of South Texas’s most important water sources, providing drinking water for families, supporting agriculture, and sustaining communities along the border. Protecting the river and planning for its long-term needs are critical to our region.

In the House-passed Water Resources Development Act of 2026, I secured three provisions to expand opportunities for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to address water and environmental challenges across the Rio Grande Basin.

These provisions make the Rio Grande Basin eligible for a comprehensive watershed assessment to identify water resource needs, allow counties along the Rio Grande to pursue future flood protection and riverbank restoration projects, and expand opportunities to address harmful algal blooms that threaten water quality and aquatic life.

These are important steps toward protecting the Rio Grande and the communities that depend on it. I will continue working to get these provisions through final passage and make sure South Texas is included in future federal water infrastructure and environmental restoration efforts.

Families in Zapata County depend on reliable water infrastructure, and communities like Medina Colonia need better protection from erosion and flooding.

In the House-passed Water Resources Development Act of 2026, I secured an increase in Zapata County’s water and wastewater infrastructure authorization from $20 million to $30 million. I also expanded the authorization to include water distribution systems, which could help improve water service and reliability for residents across the county.

The bill also directs the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to expedite flood protection work in Medina Colonia. This is an important step toward addressing long-standing concerns about erosion and protecting the homes and families affected.

I will continue working to get these provisions through final passage and secure the federal funding needed to improve water infrastructure and strengthen flood protection in Zapata County.

My Outreach Coordinator, Kelly Brooks, recently joined a luncheon hosted by the Pleasanton Public Library featuring a silent auction to raise funds for additional resources and support for library programs and activities.

Public libraries provide access to books, educational resources, technology, engaging programs, and opportunities for lifelong learning. Events like this highlight the importance of community involvement in ensuring these valuable resources remain accessible to all.

Thank you to the Pleasanton Public Library’s continued commitment to education, learning, and community engagement.

The national average gas price has exceeded $4 per gallon on 158 days this year, setting a new record for the most days above $4 in a single year.

For families across South Texas, these costs add up quickly. Whether it is driving to work, taking children to school, or running a small business, higher fuel prices are taking more money out of household budgets. Truck drivers, farmers, and ranchers are also paying more to operate, which can lead to higher prices for the goods and services families depend on every day.

According to Moody’s Analytics chief economist Mark Zandi, the war in Iran has cost the average American household nearly $2,000 through higher energy prices, borrowing costs, and military spending. That is a significant financial burden at a time when families are already dealing with higher costs for groceries, housing, and other everyday necessities.

Congress needs to take the economic consequences of this war seriously. Families across South Texas are already paying more at the pump and for everyday necessities. We need to focus on lowering energy costs and providing relief to the families and businesses dealing with these higher prices.

Families across Starr County depend on reliable water service, and communities like Roma and Escobares have dealt with flooding for years.

In the House-passed Water Resources Development Act of 2026, I secured a $7.5 million authorization for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to support water and wastewater infrastructure improvements in Starr County, including improvements to water supply and distribution systems.

The bill also authorizes the Army Corps to study flood risks in Roma and Escobares and identify potential solutions to reduce flooding. These studies are an important first step toward protecting homes, roads, and businesses from future flood damage.

I will continue working to get these provisions through final passage and secure the federal funding needed to improve water infrastructure and address flooding in Starr County.

Last Friday, my Outreach Coordinator, Kassandra Herrera, attended the Business Expo Laredo 2026 Press Conference and Exhibitors’ VIP Dinner at the Falcon Bank Event Center.

This event provided an opportunity to engage with local business owners, exhibitors, and community members and celebrate their contributions to Laredo’s business community.

My office is grateful for opportunities like these that foster connections, strengthen community partnerships, and celebrate the spirit of local business in Laredo.

Families in Jim Hogg County depend on reliable water infrastructure for their homes, businesses, and everyday needs.

In the House-passed Water Resources Development Act of 2026, I secured a $7.5 million authorization for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to support water infrastructure improvements in Jim Hogg County.

This authorization could help replace aging water lines, reduce water loss, and improve the reliability of the county’s water distribution system. These improvements are important for ensuring residents have access to safe, dependable drinking water.

This is an important step for Jim Hogg County, but we still need to secure the funding to make these improvements a reality. I will continue working to get this legislation through final passage and bring federal water infrastructure investments back to South Texas.

Today, I was pleased to announce $210,000 in federal funding through the U.S. Economic Development Administration’s Partnership Planning Program to support the South Texas Development Council’s regional economic development efforts in Webb, Zapata, Jim Hogg and Starr counties.

This funding will help STDC update and implement the region’s Comprehensive Economic Development Strategy - a roadmap for supporting job creation, workforce development, infrastructure improvements and business growth.

It will also support planning and technical assistance for local communities, helping leaders coordinate development projects and pursue additional resources. This assistance is especially valuable for rural communities with limited planning resources.

Congratulations and thank you to Juan Rodriguez and the STDC team for your continued dedication to South Texas! I’ll continue working to bring federal resources home to help our communities grow and expand opportunities for residents across our region.

Last night, I was pleased to join @LULAC Council #12 for the 2026 Tejano Achievers Awards Dinner, celebrating ten outstanding community leaders and professionals whose accomplishments and service have made a meaningful difference in Laredo.

I also had the honor of presenting Congressional Recognitions to these community leaders in appreciation of their professional achievements, leadership and dedication to serving others.

Congratulations to all of this year’s Tejano Achievers! Thank you to LULAC Council #12 for recognizing the individuals who continue to strengthen Laredo and South Texas.

Today, I was proud to announce $938,000 in federal Community Project Funding for renovations to the Hebbronville Community Center. I secured this funding through the FY2027 appropriations process, and it is included in the appropriations bill.

The Community Center is an important gathering place for Jim Hogg County residents, hosting public events, community meetings, and the County Fair. These funds would support a new roof, structural improvements, an upgraded HVAC system, a commercial kitchen, and essential plumbing, electrical, and restroom upgrades. The improvements would also strengthen the facility’s ability to serve as an emergency shelter during hurricanes, flooding, and other disasters.

This investment builds on the $1.285 million secured for Kohler Park improvements and $1 million for the Jim Hogg County Emergency Response Center. Together, these projects support community recreation, public safety, and emergency preparedness throughout the county.

Today, I was proud to announce the Community Water and Energy Resource Center (CWERC) Feasibility Study, an important initiative that will explore innovative solutions to strengthen Laredo’s water supply, improve wastewater treatment, and expand renewable energy opportunities.

The proposed facility would reclaim and reuse wastewater, transform organic waste into renewable energy, and help create a more sustainable and locally controlled water resource for our community. If determined feasible, the facility could potentially recycle 2 to 3 million gallons of wastewater per day, helping reduce our dependence on the Rio Grande while meeting Laredo’s growing water needs.

This initiative is supported by $180,000 in federal funding from the North American Development Bank’s Technical Assistance Program, along with $81,500 in additional funding from RGISC, the City of Laredo, Harvard Graduate School of Design, and Zimmerman Consulting, bringing the total project investment to $261,500.

Beyond strengthening our water supply, this project could create economic opportunities, support local job creation, provide reclaimed water for businesses and irrigation, and recover valuable resources from waste. The feasibility study will evaluate the project’s engineering, environmental benefits, potential locations, and economic viability to help determine the best path forward.

I look forward to continuing our partnership with NADBank, RGISC, the City of Laredo, and our other partners to advance innovative solutions that protect our natural resources, strengthen our long-term water security, and support Laredo’s continued growth. Planning for our future means investing in sustainable solutions that will benefit our community for generations to come.

Laredo is growing, and our water and wastewater infrastructure needs to keep up with the needs of our community.

In the House-passed Water Resources Development Act of 2026, I secured a $25 million authorization for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to support water and wastewater infrastructure improvements in Laredo.

This authorization could help replace aging water lines, reduce water loss, strengthen our water supply, and improve drainage in neighborhoods that experience repeated flooding. It could also support environmental restoration projects that help protect our waterways and reduce flood risks.

This is an important step toward improving Laredo’s water infrastructure, but there is still work to be done. I will continue working to get this legislation across the finish line and secure the federal funding needed to move these projects forward.

Small businesses across South Texas are dealing with higher costs and growing uncertainty, making it harder for owners to pay their employees, invest in their businesses, and plan for the future.

A new survey of 1,171 small business owners by Small Business for America’s Future found that 64% have cut or skipped their own pay to keep their businesses running. Many are also delaying investments because of uncertainty surrounding federal economic policies.

For small businesses in South Texas, tariffs and rising operating costs affect everything from purchasing supplies to hiring workers. These businesses support local jobs, provide important services, and contribute to our communities.

I will continue working across the aisle to lower costs, support predictable trade policies, and make sure our small businesses have the opportunity to compete and grow.

Originally from Mexico City, Andrea is a senior at the University of Texas at San Antonio, where she is majoring in marketing. After graduation, she hopes to pursue a career in corporate marketing.

Thank you, Andrea, for your hard work and dedication to our constituents. We appreciate having you as part of our team, and I wish you all the best as you finish your studies and pursue your career goals. Congratulations!

My office recently helped deliver a book donation from the Library of Congress to the Pleasanton Public Library!

Outreach Coordinator Kelly Brooks joined Library Director Gina Steward to celebrate the donation and help provide more reading and educational materials for the community.

Local libraries play an important role in helping students learn, encouraging children to read, and providing families with access to books and other resources.

Thank you to Gina and the Pleasanton Public Library staff for the work they do to support literacy and education in Atascosa County. I will continue working to connect our local libraries with federal resources that benefit our communities.

Inflation moved in the wrong direction in September. Consumer prices rose 3.7% over the past year, up from 3.4% in August, while gasoline prices jumped 9.1% in just one month.

For families across South Texas, higher fuel prices mean more than paying extra at the pump. Truck drivers, farmers, ranchers, and small businesses are also dealing with higher operating costs, which can lead to higher prices for the goods and services families depend on every day.

Families are already stretching their paychecks to cover groceries, housing, utilities, and health care. Congress needs to focus on bringing these costs down and providing relief to working families and small businesses.

I will continue working with Republicans and Democrats to address rising costs, support South Texas workers and businesses, and help families keep more of their hard-earned money.

Behind every grant is a student working toward a brighter future. 

As an author of the TEXAS Grant Program during my time in the Texas Legislature, I’m proud to see its lasting impact.

Hear from Dahlia Vasquez and Silvia Silva about how TEXAS and Pell Grants have supported their college journeys at TAMIU and Laredo College.

I’ll continue working to make higher education more affordable for South Texas families.

For many families in South Texas, school breakfast and lunch programs help make sure their children have nutritious meals while easing the cost of groceries at home.

In the FY27 House Agriculture Appropriations bill, I helped secure $37.9 billion for Child Nutrition programs, including the National School Lunch Program, School Breakfast Program, and Summer Food Programs.

These programs help provide students with healthy meals throughout the school year and during the summer months when school is out. They also provide important support for working parents and families who are already dealing with high food costs.

Children should be able to focus on learning, not worrying about their next meal. As a senior member of the House Appropriations Committee, I will continue working to protect these programs and make sure South Texas families have access to the resources they depend on.

It is great to see this mother-daughter team working together to grow their businesses. Small businesses are an important part of Laredo’s economy, and it is always good to see local entrepreneurs investing in our community.

Congratulations to Yuliana and Gloria on this milestone! I wish them both continued success and encourage the Laredo community to stop by and support these local businesses.

More Texans will now have access to federal Pell Grants to help pay for short-term job training programs.

Five Texas community colleges have been approved to offer eligible Workforce Pell programs, including Texas Southmost College in Brownsville. These programs will help students train for careers in fields like welding, health care, HVAC, and machining.

I supported expanding Pell Grant eligibility to include short-term trade and workforce training programs because students should have access to federal financial assistance whether they are pursuing a college degree or learning a skilled trade. This change will help more Texans gain the skills they need for good-paying jobs.

I encourage eligible Texans to explore these opportunities by completing the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) at https://t.co/8wv08KYFRt and contacting a participating college to learn more.

I also encourage other colleges across South Texas to seek approval for their workforce training programs so more students in our region can benefit from this federal assistance. Expanding access to affordable education and job training is important for our students, workers, and local economy.

https://t.co/0y4eqYXfWD

The cost of living remains a major concern for families across South Texas. Groceries, housing, utilities, and health care continue to take a large share of household budgets, and many Americans are worried about their financial future.

A new poll found that nearly four in ten Americans believe they would be worse off financially if Republicans maintain control of Congress. These concerns should be taken seriously. Families want to know they can afford their everyday expenses and have some financial security.

Congress needs to focus on lowering costs, protecting Medicare and Social Security, and supporting good-paying jobs. Families who work hard every day should not have to worry about whether their paycheck will cover their basic needs.

I will continue working across the aisle to address the cost of living, support our small businesses, and make sure the needs of South Texas families are heard in Washington.

post.text:
The House passed the bipartisan Major Richard Star Act (H.R. 2102) yesterday morning, which I supported to end the “wounded veteran tax.”

Combat-injured veterans who were forced to medically retire should not have to choose between their military retirement pay and VA disability compensation. This bill would allow eligible veterans to receive both benefits in full.

Our veterans have earned these benefits through their service and sacrifice. I urge the Senate to pass this legislation so we can get it signed into law.
